findings.description: `isNewGap` counts a gap as new even when it comes from an adapter the previous capture never detected. A TS repo that adds a `pyproject.toml` without vulture therefore refuses every `pup audit` and `--sweep`, while protecting a dead-code figure that never had a Python share.

On a baseline with no `gaps` field (every existing project on its first audit after upgrade), a coverage failure no longer blocks. The run stores no `coverageRatio` and records `('<adapter>', 'coverage')` in `gaps`, so from then on that gap counts as already known and is never refused again: the figure is lost for good. A legacy fallback such as `return gap.capability === 'coverage' && previous.debt?.coverageRatio !== undefined` would keep the old protection.

The inline `{ adapterId: string; capability: string }[]` on `ProjectBaseline.gaps` restates the first two fields of `DebtGap` in `src/core/types/debt.types.ts`. Declaring it as `Pick<DebtGap, 'adapterId' | 'capability'>[]` would keep one source of truth for the field names.
The refusal branch re-implements the drift loop that `printBaselineTail` already runs on `debtTransitions`, so the same drift lines now have two print sites that can diverge in indent or format.
